IEE Colloquium on TickIT Certification Initiative: Objectives and Practice
abstract: DTI has had an involvement with the UK IT industry since 1982 and over the course of time, their approach has changed from supporting single companies and research and development of new products, to programmes like Alvey and the promotion of standards and best practice. To help the IT industry, the Department's IT Division established the Software Quality Unit (SQU) with the purpose of improving the quality of software in the UK by encouraging the use of best practice and appropriate standards and certification. SQU provides support for strengthening of the certification scheme for quality management systems applied to software design and development. Work is in hand to enhance these arrangements and this scheme is called TickIT. The DTI involvement in this significant project is discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The TickIT initiative a purchaser's perspective (software certification)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on TickIT Certification Initiative: Objectives and Practice
abstract: TickIT is a software certification scheme for ensuring software quality, set up by the UK government. The author describes the MOD (Ministry of Defence) interest in this initiative. Past efforts by the MOD for acquiring quality software are outlined and the importance of this for military applications is emphasised.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on TickIT Certification Initiative: Objectives and Practice
abstract: The third party assessment to BS5750 of the quality management systems within supplier organisations is a UK-wide activity covering thousands of companies. Until two years ago (1989), the IT companies amongst those thousands numbered a few dozen and included software producing companies which could be counted on the fingers of one hand. The author gives the reasons for this and explains why software certification and TickIT have gained popularity. The assessment of a company (SD-Scicon UK) who wished to acquire accreditation from the TickIT certification scheme and ISO 9001/BS5750 is described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on TickIT Certification Initiative: Objectives and Practice
abstract: In the UK there are national procedures for the granting of authoritative certificates to organizations who can demonstrate effective quality management in line with international standards. The author explains how the Department of Trade and Industry have been working with industry to extend these procedures to the software and IT sector. Whilst TickIT is a certification scheme, this is not the main goal. The principal objective is to stimulate developers to think about what quality really is and how it may be achieved. Unless certification is purely a byproduct of the more fundamental aim of delivering quality, much of the effort will be wasted. To stimulate thinking, TickIT includes some quality themes which set out the context within which quality management systems (QMS) certification should be perceived.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The TickIT initiative-how the certifier works (software reliability)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on TickIT Certification Initiative: Objectives and Practice
abstract: BSI Quality Assurance is the certification business of the British Standards Institution. They believe that they are the largest and most active third-party certification body in the world. The author describes the role of BSI QA in software quality assurance and in the TickIT software certification scheme. He also examines the involvement of BSI QA in the establishment of accreditation criteria for certification of software developers.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
